chunks: Do not kill the Kharijites after me
because one who seeks right but does not find it, is not like one who seeks wrong and finds it.

key_terms.الْخَوَارِجَ: The Kharijites, a early Islamic sect known for their rebellion and distinct theological views

ai.seo_question: What is the theological principle behind not killing the Kharijites?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) uses this maxim to justify the strategic leniency shown during the Battle of Nahrawan, distinguishing the Kharijites as 'people of error' (ahl al-bida') rather than 'people of disbelief' (ahl al-kufr) due to their sincere but misguided pursuit of truth. This theological nuance prevents the premature excommunication (takfir) of early Muslims and underscores the Shia principle that judicial ruling (hukm) applies to those who err in their ijtihad, preserving communal unity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Do not fight [1] the Khārijites after me,
because one who seeks right but does not find it, is not like one who seeks wrong and finds it.
